claim_one_line: B1260'S DECIDING COMPUTATION, RUN: THE INDEX IS ZERO AND THE NON-SELF-DUAL RANK-3 COMPONENTS ARE RIGID. B1260 named the computation and did not run it, and this seat then listed it as a requirement rather than executing it -- which the owner called out. B1260's stakes, in its own words: 'Differ => the cusped manifold carries net chirality and JOIN 1's first question resolves in favour of the cusped object. Agree => the wall extends past closedness AND past the abelian sector, and the generation count cannot be a net-chirality count on this manifold at all.' THE ANSWER IS AGREE. SETUP: m004 is a once-punctured-torus bundle so pi_1 = <a,b,t | t a t^-1 phi(a)^-1, t b t^-1 phi(b)^-1> with phi: a->aab, b->ab, and Fox calculus on that 3-generator/2-relator presentation gives h1 directly, with the dual local system rho*(g) = rho(g^-1)^T; B71's realize/monodromy supply A, B, t. THE CONTROL CAUGHT A REAL BUG: validated against tonight's independently verified knot-group Fox table (B1256 addendum, two primes) the machinery reproduces Sym^1->0, Sym^2->1, Sym^3->0, Sym^4->1, Sym^6->1, five for five -- but a FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED it with relator residuals 1.1 to 9.3 because the Sym^n routine returned the TRANSPOSE, making Sym an ANTI-homomorphism and destroying the relations; without the control the wrong answer would have shipped, and a homomorphism check now runs before any result is used. THE RESULT over 25 valid parameter points per component: V0 (self-dual, geometric) gives h1 in {0,1} with INDEX always 0; W1 and W2 (NON-self-dual) give h1 = 0 always with INDEX always 0 and smallest d1 singular values 0.011 and 0.020, far from zero, so rank 6 is numerically solid. V0 ATTAINING h1 = 1 is what makes this a test rather than a tautology. TWO CONCLUSIONS: (1) the index is ZERO everywhere tested, so by B1260's own statement the wall extends past closedness and past the abelian sector; (2) W1 and W2 are RIGID with no deformations at all, so they carry no massless modes and cannot furnish a generation count in EITHER direction -- the last candidate locus is not merely index-zero, it is EMPTY of the modes a count would have to count. DOES NOT say net chirality is impossible on m004 for every local system, only for the corpus's exhibited non-self-dual rank-3 family over the sampled range; a non-rigid non-self-dual system elsewhere would reopen it. ADDENDUM 2026-09-06 -- THE OBSTRUCTION IS NOT RANK, IT IS GENERIC RIGIDITY. The arc named 'a non-rigid non-self-dual system' as its revival path, so the search went up in rank: irreducible SL(n,C) reps of pi_1(m004) solved directly from the mapping-torus relations for n = 2..6, ten per rank. A control passes on the way -- n = 2 returns ZERO non-self-dual reps, exactly right since every SL(2) rep is self-dual. 34 NON-SELF-DUAL reps found across ranks 3-6, and EVERY ONE IS RIGID (h^1 = 0); the index is 0 at all 50. So going up in rank does NOT help, because RIGIDITY IS GENERIC AT EVERY RANK and a random solver only lands on generic points. THE DICHOTOMY THIS EXPOSES: the non-rigid systems we know (Sym^n of the geometric holonomy, h^1 = 1 by MFP, reproduced 5/5 in the parent arc) are SELF-DUAL, so index 0 BY DUALITY; the non-self-dual systems we find are RIGID, so index 0 FOR LACK OF MODES. Either way the index vanishes, but for two structurally different reasons and neither is a cancellation. CORRECTS THE REVIVAL PATH: not higher rank, but SPECIAL LOCI -- the modes live at measure-zero points and no random search reaches them, so a revival must CONSTRUCT a non-self-dual system at a special locus rather than sample for one. Honest scope: a search over 50 representations, not a theorem.
